# Incise 0.4.0

## Confirmed whole-table deletion

Incise 0.4.0 adds `incise table-delete`, a byte-preserving CLI operation for removing one complete Markdown table. Address the table by heading and optional ordinal. The first unconfirmed call resolves the target, reports its row count, columns, and bounded first/last row preview, then writes nothing. Repeat with `--confirm` only after verifying the target.

The splice deletes only the table lines and one separating blank-line gap. It normally takes the trailing gap; at end of file or immediately before the next section, it takes the leading gap instead. Headings, captions, section subtrees, neighbouring tables, and all other bytes remain untouched. Non-rectangular tables can be removed because whole-table deletion does not reinterpret their cells.

## Model schemas stay unchanged

Whole-table deletion is CLI-only in this release. Pi and Hermes retain the measured four-action `table_edit` schema and their existing standard and fallback surfaces.

Three preregistered MiniCPM5 candidate populations scored 50/60, 59/60, and 59/60. Across all 180 trials there was no data loss, silent corruption, collateral deletion, or wrong-table deletion, but every candidate missed the required 60/60 confirmation-recovery gate. Incise therefore ships the safe executor without publishing an action models did not use reliably enough.

## Install

Install the Rust CLI with:

```bash
cargo install incise-cli --version 0.4.0 --locked
```

Install Pi with `pi install npm:pi-incise`. Download the version-matched Hermes archive from this release, extract it into the Hermes plugin directory, and run `hermes plugins doctor --ci incise`. Pi and Hermes package 0.4.0 because their native distributions include the new CLI binary even though their model tool schemas are unchanged.

## Validation and artifacts

The Rust workspace, independent Python oracle, CLI and adapter suites, schema pin, replay consistency checks, and Pi/Hermes integration tests pass. The differential suite agrees across 122,307 generated cases over 60 fixtures, and all six targeted whole-table-deletion mutations are caught.

The tag publishes `incise-core` and `incise-cli`, four platform CLI archives, four native npm packages, `pi-incise`, and the version-matched Hermes plugin archive. Stable npm packages publish under `latest`. GitHub release assets include SHA-256 checksums.
